correctness.rationale: Polar beta norms and the Bergman kernel series give an exact finite-rank anti-diagonal singular multiset. Stirling ratio bounds yield a uniform two-endpoint majorant and the fixed-index edge law. Riemann sums, harmonic summation and dominated convergence prove all three Schatten regimes; bulk maximization or fixed-edge estimates give operator norm. The specified definitions and critical coefficient were independently algebraically reconstructed; supplementary check.py passed 124 finite diagnostics.

originality.rationale: The new statement is an exact full monomial singular multiset and three sharp Schatten mass asymptotics in an independently kernel-weighted Besov Hilbert norm. The motivating paper proves qualitative boundedness under parameter restrictions, and the located related results concern big rather than small Hankel leakage or other operator types. Older exact specializations remain a genuine priority risk because Janson 1988 full text was inaccessible.
residual_risks: An older equivalent exact monomial spectral formula under weighted Bergman/Besov coefficient norms may subsume the statement; Janson 1988 and Arazy--Fisher--Peetre 1988 full texts were not available for a decisive comparison.
The motivating preprint does not print a primary MSC: 47B35 is an independently justified subject classification for this new finding, not purported author metadata.

value.rationale: A natural high-degree symbol family in the current Hilbert Besov small-Hankel setting has a sharp qualitative-to-quantitative gap: three distinct Schatten growth laws with explicit constants, an exponent-dependent logarithmic threshold, and a sharp operator norm bulk/edge transition exactly where the general-symbol kernel hypothesis ceases to apply. This distinguishes the precise finite-rank invariant from routine boundedness or known big-Hankel profiles.
